newsitem.title: HONG KONG: S&P does not foresee China rating change for years.
newsitem.headline: S&P does not foresee China rating change for years.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp said on Friday it does not foresee a change in China's sovereign rating for at least the next several years.

"We think that it is important to indicate that for at least the next several years (China's rating) is not expected to change until we learn a bit more about what is entailed in the adjustment process," S&P said in a conference call.
S&P on Wednesday raised China's foreign currency credit rating to BBB-plus from BBB. It also revised the country's ratings outlook to stable from positive.

S&P said China has made remarkable progress in reforming and modernising its monetary management system but was still in a process of transition. As such, China remains vulnerable to shocks in the system, it said.
China has been moving towards affecting monetary policy with indirect tools rather than by credit allocation, but more needs to be done, S&P said.
For example, China must move towards open market operations to affect interest rates, it said.
"We think that over the next couple of years we will know better how these challenges can be met. So we think it best to sit back and see how China is able to cope," S&P said.
If "everything goes according to schedule" then China could be raised to a single-A credit rating, S&P said.
